statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and do not reopen inside this horizon, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any published hour and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor, while Stress stays in the elevated band on the verified Saturday US-Iran tanker exchange, a 10% weekly crude gain and hawkish rate repricing after the August payroll beat.
recommendation: Tail holds a closed-venue floor of 4-5% across all 24 published hours, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green throughout. Stress opens at 51% and drifts to a 58% peak, inside the elevated band for the whole horizon, reflecting Saturday's verified US-Iran exchange and the CENTCOM threat to Iran's oil fleet, an impaired Strait of Hormuz with WTI up close to 10% on the week, hawkish September rate pricing after a 162,000 August payroll print, an unpriced Friday trade-embargo ultimatum tied to Fed policy, and a data-heavy week containing August PPI on 10 September and August CPI on 11 September. Tail remains far below the block threshold; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through the CME weekend halt as the verified US-Iran tanker exchange stays unresolved, crude holds a near-10% weekly gain, and Labor Day pushes the first US cash session out to 8 September
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle and do not reopen within this horizon, so the last print is the only anchor and no hour of the published forecast can contain observable price action. The verified Saturday sequence remains the dominant unresolved input. NBC News reports that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer, that both vessels evaded and no US personnel were harmed, and that US forces permanently disabled the tankers M/T Downy off Kharg Island and M/T Stark 1 near Jask and destroyed M/T Kylo in the Gulf of Oman after its crew was evacuated. CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper said the response imposed a higher economic cost and that US forces would if necessary destroy Iran's limited and exposed oil fleet. Iranian state media confirmed the Kharg strike without reporting casualties, and no Iranian state response or Strait of Hormuz closure announcement has been verified at the time of this assessment. Reuters reports WTI settling at 91.48 dollars and Brent at 96.28 dollars on Friday, with WTI up close to 10% on the week and US diesel at a record 5.85 dollars per gallon. The macro backdrop is separately two-sided. August payrolls rose 162,000 against a consensus near 53,000 with unemployment steady at 4.1% and annual wage growth at 3.1%, lifting the 10-year Treasury yield roughly three basis points to 4.79% with the 2-year near 4.37% and raising published odds of a September rate increase, while several outlets describe the decision as hinging on the 11 September CPI release. On Friday the President also tied a threatened trade embargo on deficit countries to a demand for Fed rate cuts, an item that remains entirely unpriced. Cross-asset context from the latest completed session is mixed rather than aligned: semiconductors and semiconductor equipment led while application and infrastructure software lagged, communication services and consumer cyclicals were negative, and the VIX closed at 14.53 within a 13.80 to 14.58 range, a low absolute volatility base. Because none of this can express itself while quoting is suspended, the unresolved stack is scored as elevated Stress with Tail held at a closed-venue floor. US Labor Day on 7 September means the first cash session after the reopen is 8 September, so the backlog carried into price discovery is longer than on a normal weekend. That consideration is published as a conditional gap risk for hours beyond this horizon, not as observed structure.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the closing four hours of the August payroll session and the first twenty hours of the CME weekend halt. The 17:00 UTC hour on 4 September was already past the release peak at Tail 14% and Stress 54% under a mixed mode, and every slot in this window maps to EA_ON and green. Tail decayed through the remainder of the US cash session as the index gave back its highs and recovered, reaching Tail 12% and Stress 48% by 20:00 UTC with semiconductor leadership diverging from a softer broad tape. From the 21:00 UTC futures settlement onward every hour has been scored at the closed-venue floor of Tail 5% with mode normal, while Stress eased to 38% and then drifted back up through the Saturday hours as the verified US-Iran exchange was reported and the unpriced weekend stack accumulated, reaching 50% at 16:00 UTC. All 24 slots carry a published Claude assessment.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, which does not end until several hours after the final published slot, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress opens at 51% and drifts to a 58% peak, inside the elevated band for the whole horizon, reflecting Saturday's verified US-Iran tanker exchange and the CENTCOM threat to Iran's oil fleet, an energy premium from continued Strait of Hormuz disruption, hawkish September rate pricing after the August payroll beat, an unresolved Friday trade-embargo ultimatum tied to Fed policy, and an open two-sided headline window whose accumulated content would express in a single reopening auction. Mode is characterised as normal through the dormant hours and mixed in the closing hours, where the setup carried toward the reopen is genuinely two-sided rather than directional. Confidence stays in the high band, easing from 85% to 79% purely as a function of evidence age across a full weekend without a refreshing quote.
